source_snapshot.procedure:
【Before Test】
    1. Check that the SUT configuration (e.g., hardware, firmware, drivers, etc.) matches the specifications/recipe definition.
    2. Clear logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.).

    【During Test】
    1. update aspeed driver to lastest
2.Change screen resolution.
   - In Linux, "Setting -> Display"
   - In Windows, click right button of mouse, select "Screen resolution"
Check all supported resolutions ( e.g. , 800x600, 1024x768, 1280x1024 )

    【After Test】
    1. Collect test results and photos, and save them to specific folders.
    2. Check if there are unexpected logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.) generate after test.
source_snapshot.criteria: Resolutions should be changed successfully and monitor should display correctly (No moire, screen flicker or color difference).

deepseek_columns.ai_commands: sshpass -p "$DUT_PASS" ssh -o StrictHostKeyChecking=no $DUT_USER@$DUT_IP "xrandr --query 2>&1; echo ---; cat /sys/class/drm/card*/modes 2>/dev/null | head 2>&1"
deepseek_columns.ai_logs_output: return FULL `xrandr --query` + DRM modes so the user confirms the VGA resolution options/current mode; actually changing the on-screen resolution is a GUI/display action needing a person to view the monitor.
deepseek_columns.risk: RISK: display tests need a physical monitor head + a person to observe rendering; agent runs the read-only/headless probe for mode/status evidence only.

original_test_intent: With the approved ASPEED display driver, select every supported VGA resolution in the required Linux and Windows GUI paths and visually verify stable, correct physical-monitor output without moire, flicker or color difference.
original_method: An engineer approves and, if required, applies a specific compatible ASPEED driver with rollback, then changes each owner-defined resolution/refresh/color mode through the OS display UI and visually inspects a known monitor; read-only DRM/xrandr evidence corroborates the selected state.
manual_activity: A person must operate/observe the physical display and judge moire, flicker and color differences for each Linux/Windows mode. Automated mode listings or screenshots cannot establish the physical rendering criterion.
required_inputs: Exact ASPEED device, current/target signed driver package/version, supported OS and rollback
Required Linux/Windows resolution, refresh, color-depth and timing matrix
Physical VGA port, monitor, cable and expected EDID/connector mapping
Qualified visual observer, console/KVM/OOB recovery and one-user approval
safety_requirements: Do not interpret 'latest' as authorization to install an unverified driver; confirm compatibility, integrity and rollback first.
Do not change driver/mode or restart display services without a recoverable console/KVM path.
Do not use xrandr/DRM enumeration as proof of visible artifact-free output.
Stop on black screen, flicker/moire/color defect, unsupported mode, EDID failure or display-driver crash and preserve logs.
No automatic retry, driver reinstall, reboot or fallback mode change.
agent_execution_scope: Prepare the approved driver/mode/OS/monitor matrix and capture read-only driver, connector, EDID and mode baselines.
Support only explicitly approved driver or mode actions and collect selected-mode/status/log evidence.
Correlate engineer observations with each exact mode and assemble recovery/restoration evidence.
Do not visually accept the display or issue the verdict.
engineer_actions: Approve the exact ASPEED driver package/version and recovery path; perform/confirm any update.
Select and visually inspect every required mode on the physical monitor in each required OS.
Restore the approved state and issue the formal verdict.

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: Useful Linux discovery only. `head` can discard required modes; it cannot change modes, cover Windows, verify driver update or judge physical artifacts. Password SSH and disabled host-key validation also require replacement.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: Preserve full untruncated approved xrandr/DRM connector/mode/EDID evidence on Linux. Use the project's validated driver and OS-native display path; no generic latest-driver command is recommended.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: Example resolutions 800x600, 1024x768 and 1280x1024, both OS paths and source times 30/30 are retained as source facts, not treated as the complete owner matrix.

modernized_recommendation.status: EXACT DRIVER/MODE MATRIX AND VISUAL ACCEPTANCE
modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Record one evidence row per OS/mode/refresh/color-depth combination with driver/connector/EDID state, selected-mode confirmation, timed visual observation and safe revert path.
modernized_recommendation.applicable_platform: The named ASPEED VGA device, OS image, physical port, cable and monitor.
modernized_recommendation.supported_version: Use and record the project-approved driver/OS/firmware versions; do not assume latest.
modernized_recommendation.official_reference: Owner compatibility/mode specification and signed driver source; not provided in the row.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Replaces ambiguous latest-driver handling with an approved version/rollback and makes the visual matrix traceable.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: Digital mode evidence supports but does not replace physical moire/flicker/color evaluation or Windows GUI coverage.
modernized_recommendation.required_inputs: Driver package/version, OS/mode matrix, monitor path, observer and recovery.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: Remote screenshots may not reveal analog VGA artifacts visible on the physical panel.

project_override_considerations: A project may approve a subset of resolutions/OSes and report only that plan's completion, with omitted source coverage explicit. Supplying a package/matrix does not change MANUAL ONLY because physical rendering judgment remains central.
expected_evidence: ASPEED device/current-target driver/package hash/compatibility/rollback and approval
Monitor/cable/port/EDID plus exact OS resolution/refresh/color matrix
Raw untruncated driver/xrandr/DRM/connector evidence and selected-mode status per test
Timestamped operator photos/notes for moire, flicker, color and stable output plus restoration logs

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: Driver preparation, OS mode changes and visual criteria consistently support VGA resolution validation. 'Latest' is unsafe/underspecified but does not contradict the test purpose.

blocked_analysis.analysis: Exact driver, matrix and observer are readiness inputs. The manual operation and visual acceptance are clear once supplied, so MANUAL ONLY is sufficient.

comparison_to_prior_reviews.deepseek: Retain its visual limitation but reject partial completion from truncated Linux mode discovery and restore driver/Windows/physical coverage.
comparison_to_prior_reviews.gpt_v2: Keep V2's driver rollback and visual matrix, but reclassify PARTIAL to MANUAL ONLY because GUI selection and physical quality judgment are core.
comparison_to_prior_reviews.v3_1_improvement: Separates risky driver readiness from manual display acceptance and engineer verdict ownership.

review_improvement: This review prevents 'latest' from triggering an uncontrolled driver update and ensures mode enumeration is not misreported as visible analog VGA quality validation.
independent_technical_reasoning: The acceptance defects—moire, flicker and color difference—occur on the physical signal/monitor path and may be absent from digital screenshots or mode status. Because the source also explicitly uses OS GUIs, the complete case requires human observation and is MANUAL ONLY.
